behavioral_notes.observation: Releasing an MO confirms its raw-material and finished stock.move records (_action_confirm), adjusts their procure_method, confirms work orders, confirms component pickings, and triggers the procurement scheduler for forecasted-short components; draft MOs transition state to 'confirmed'. The downstream document chain is created via stock, invisible in metadata.

Completing an MO posts inventory: raw-material moves are consumed via stock.move._action_done (decrementing component quants), finished/byproduct moves are produced into the destination location, work-order durations are finalized and order._cal_price assigns the manufacturing cost (component cost + workcenter cost) to the produced goods, updating stock valuation. State becomes 'done' and the order is locked.

Explodes a BoM for a given quantity, recursively resolving phantom (kit) sub-BoMs via _bom_find(bom_type='phantom'), producing the component and operation lists that seed an MO's move_raw_ids and workorders. Pure Python recursion not derivable from field metadata.

The 'manufacture' stock.rule action (wired on stock.warehouse via manufacture_pull_id) reacts to a procurement by finding the matching BoM (_get_matching_bom) and creating an mrp.production via _prepare_mo_vals. This is how a sale order / reordering rule / MTO demand auto-spawns a production order.

Scheduling explodes operations into work orders, links operation dependencies (blocked_by_workorder_ids) and moves to work orders, then reserves finite workcenter capacity by allocating resource.calendar.leaves slots back-to-front from the final operation, setting MO date_start/date_finished.

Starting/finishing a work order writes mrp.workcenter.productivity time logs (productive vs. loss buckets) that feed the workcenter OEE/performance KPIs; durations recorded here drive the labor-cost portion applied at _post_inventory.

information_flows: side-effect: mrp.production.action_confirm -> confirms stock.move (raw + finished) + work orders + component pickings
side-effect: mrp.production.button_mark_done/_post_inventory -> consumes component quants + produces finished/byproduct quants + stock valuation (component + workcenter cost)
side-effect: mrp.workorder time logs -> mrp.workcenter.productivity -> OEE/performance KPIs

capabilities: Define Bills of Material (incl. kits/phantom & byproducts)
value_streams: Plan-to-Produce: procurement/demand -> MO created (manufacture rule) -> scheduled (work orders) -> released (action_confirm reserves components) -> executed (work orders) -> marked done (_post_inventory consumes raw, produces finished, values output)
policies: 9 record rules: multi-company scoping on MO/BoM/workcenter documents
consumption policy (flexible/warning/strict) enforces component over/under-use via mrp.consumption.warning
BoM 'ready_to_produce' policy (all components / when components available)
manufacture_steps warehouse policy (1/2/3-step manufacturing with PBM/SAM locations)

classification.rationale: mrp is the Operations transform step of the value chain (Stabell & Fjeldstad 'chain'): it consumes raw-material inputs and converts them, via routed work-center operations, into finished-goods output, updating inventory and valuation. It is a primary activity that sits between procurement (inbound) and stock delivery (outbound). Per apqc_odoo_map.tsv it maps to APQC 4.3 Produce/Manufacture, specifically 4.3.1.4 (schedule production orders and create lots: mrp.production create/schedule) and 4.3.1.7 (release production orders: mrp.production.action_confirm).

standard_capabilities: multi-level BoMs with kits (phantom) and byproducts
routings with work centers, operations and operation dependencies
finite-capacity scheduling (work orders against workcenter calendars)
lot/serial tracking of components and finished goods
manufacturing cost roll-up (material + workcenter) into valuation
typical_fits: make-to-stock and make-to-order manufacturing driven by reordering rules or sale orders
shop-floor work-order execution with time tracking
common_gaps: MPS / master production scheduling (separate module mrp_mps)
custom co-product cost-share or yield models
drive_hints: odoo shell: mo = env['mrp.production'].create({'product_id': p.id, 'product_qty': 1, 'bom_id': b.id}); mo.action_confirm(); mo.state  # observe component stock.move confirmation
odoo shell --log-handler=odoo.sql_db:DEBUG: mo.button_mark_done()  # trace raw-material consumption + finished-goods valuation moves
